name: postquant
description: A post-quantum L1 whose entire state machine is a market in key/value space, with pluggable post-quantum key types where the algorithm IS a wasm module. Signatures come from two families that share nothing — ML-DSA 44/65/87 (FIPS 204, module lattices) and SLH-DSA-SHAKE-128f (FIPS 205, nothing but SHAKE256) — chosen per wallet, with the address committing to the choice; every commitment is SHA3-256 and there is no elliptic curve anywhere in the trust path. Every transaction witness is verified INSIDE the compiled wasm verifier registered for its key type (blob SHA3-256 committed in src/pq/wasm/manifest.json, checked on both sides of the process boundary, fail closed), so what a valid signature means is pinned to exact bytes any node can hash, ship and re-run — and a future key type is one plugin file plus one blob, not a fork. There is one thing to own on this chain, a key in the store, and the whole protocol is the market for it: write gas per byte (a key byte costs 4x a value byte, hash values below blobs), witness gas per byte of signature billed per scheme as-is (2420 for ML-DSA-44, 17088 for SLH-DSA — the honest price of resting on nothing but hashes), and rent per byte-hour against a prepaid escrow. Expiry makes entries sweepable for their bond; the fee market is EIP-1559 over state growth. Consensus is modular: the rule for who extends the chain is a pluggable engine — authority, rotating PoA, BFT quorum, proof of stake (SHA3 stake lottery) or SHA3 proof of work, or a plugin in src/consensus.d/ — every seal and vote is a signature under one of the chain's post-quantum key types (validators may mix them), and switching engines is a migration written into a block header and authorised by the engine it replaces, so the chain never forks and verify replays every block from genesis, rebuilds the engine schedule from the log and re-runs every witness through its key type's wasm. Contracts are stored public by hash and RUN OFF CHAIN WITH PROOF: a wasm contract exporting the pqc1 ABI (an importless pure state transition pqc_run(state,input)->state) is executed by its owner, who signs a pqr1 receipt {code, state_in, input, state_out, prev} with their post-quantum wallet and anchors it at contract/<name>/receipt; anyone verifies by fetching the blobs by hash and re-running — counter and ledger examples ship. How a step is accepted is the machine owner's customizable proof policy: replay, a custom importless wasm verifier (the pqp1 ABI, pqp_verify(state_in,input,state_out,proof)), or a k-of-n quorum of post-quantum attestations, so a state machine that is not wasm, or too heavy to re-run, is verified from a succinct proof instead. REST, the browser console, 36 MCP tools and a plain-English agent (the fleet agent contract: GET /agents + POST /run/stream) on one port, off the same functions. Key types are a market: prims (builtin, plugin or anyone's importless wasm blob) combine into key types with all / any / threshold k-of-n, and the key type market shelves both with author, uses, forks and break cost — publishing anchors keytype/<name> on chain, so authorship is a key you can list and sell. Private key types hide the scheme entirely: the address commits to SHA3(key type, salt, pk) and every witness is a fixed-size ML-KEM-768 envelope only the proposer opens, so an attacker never learns which algorithm to attack or sees a public key to attack it with. A third, independent wall: CAIRO-MSS-SHA256 rests on SHA-256 alone and its verifier is a Cairo program (STARK-provable) — stack it with ML-DSA and SLH-DSA in an ALL composite and a quantum forger must break lattices, SHAKE and SHA-256; the builder can forge any key type straight into a private wallet. Off-chain data goes to a VAULT that encrypts on the client (AES-256-GCM, PQV1 envelope) before any node sees it — nodes hold ciphertext under cid = SHA3-256(blob), the chain holds the cid as a rent-paying key, and the blob lives as long as an anchor does; smart contracts are stored the same way, public and content-addressed, behind an owned contract/<name> key.
backend: python stdlib only (http.server + hashlib) — no dependencies; ML-DSA, SLH-DSA and ML-KEM implemented in src/pq/, witness verification in per-algorithm wasm (dependency-free Rust, bare rustc, run by a node host)
frontend: src/console.html — HOME (hero front door: live chain strip, three doors, and FIRST KEY IN 60 SECONDS — a guided journey that forges a wallet, faucets it, quotes, writes a key and shows the Merkle proof, every step a real transaction), the tip, ASK (the agent), the store, the market, write/quote, BUILDER (compact parts picker grouped lattice/hash/cairo/classical/forged, QUANTUM-HARD preset, make-it-private switch; full DAG behind a fold), CONSENSUS (CHAIN ▸ Consensus: active engine + validators, one-click switch to any engine with mixed PQ key types, history of engines), wallets with per-scheme creation, the key-type table, VAULT (encrypt a file in the browser, store ciphertext, anchor, open by share link; store/show contracts), the whitepaper with live figures (security bits classical vs quantum, witness bytes, fee-market simulation, vault vs on-chain cost) and a design comparison; MARKET (the key type marketplace), PRIMS (the atoms + add a wasm prim), PRIVATE (hide your key type, prove, verify); CTRL-K command palette jumps anywhere, runs anything, and falls through to the agent; click-to-copy addresses and roots with toasts; served at /postquant
state: ~/.mod/postquant — keys.json (32-byte seeds, mode 0600, never committed), <chain_id>/blocks.jsonl (the log, the truth), <chain_id>/state.json (a snapshot, discarded if it disagrees with the log)

crypto.signatures: pluggable per account: ML-DSA-44/65/87 (FIPS 204, src/pq/mldsa.py) and SLH-DSA-SHAKE-128f (FIPS 205, src/pq/slhdsa.py); registry src/pq/algos.py, plugins in src/pq/algos.d/
crypto.verification: every witness runs inside the wasm verifier registered for its key type — src/pq/wasmvm.py + src/pq/wasm/manifest.json (SHA3-256 per blob, fail closed); Rust sources + parity tests in src/pq/wasm-src/
crypto.hash: SHA3-256 everywhere: addresses, tx ids, Merkle roots, commitments
crypto.addresses: pq + first 20 bytes of SHA3-256 over (algorithm domain, public key) — the address commits to the key type
crypto.quantum_gate: complexity-priced: any key type witnesses, classical included, if its best-known classical attack clears the 2^100 brute-force floor (maximal-entropy seed) and plugin schemes pass the entropy probe (src/pq/complexity.py); quantum cost is printed per scheme (pq_complexity / GET /complexity) - polynomial for quantum_safe=false - and POSTQUANT_REQUIRE_PQ=1 restores the strict quantum-only gate
crypto.composites: src/pq/compose.py — composite key types built out of registered ones and stored in <data dir>/keytypes.json: op=all is the hybrid AND (every part signs, falls only if every part falls, quantum-safe if any part is), op=any the 1-of-n OR (weakest link), op=threshold k-of-n (falls when the k weakest fall); parts may be composites, so key types form a DAG (pq_keytype_dag); the gate probes a composite like any plugin and pq_keytype_test runs the full proof battery
crypto.prims: pq_prims / pq_prim — the atoms key types are built from: builtin, plugin (src/pq/algos.d/) or wasm (src/pq/wasmtype.py, admitted by proof battery + determinism double-run + complexity gate)
crypto.private: src/pq/private.py — scheme 'private': address commits to SHA3(inner, salt, pk); witness = ML-KEM-768 envelope (seal key <data dir>/seal.key, never rotated) padded to POSTQUANT_SEAL_BYTES (64 KiB) so every hidden scheme is indistinguishable; the proposer opens and runs the inner verifier + gate; pq_private verify returns the proposer's signed attestation; trust: the proposer can see the scheme; pq_keytype create private=true forges and hides in one step
crypto.market: pq_keymarket — every prim/composite/private on one shelf; authorship anchor = chain key keytype/<name> = SHA3(spec), written by the author wallet on publish=true
crypto.cairo: src/pq/cairomss.py + src/pq/cairo/src/lib.cairo — CAIRO-MSS-SHA256: SPHINCS-shaped WOTS hypertree over SHA-256 (4x6 layers, 2^24 leaves, pk 64B, sig 9376B), verifier in Cairo 2; pq_cairo check runs it in the Cairo VM (scarb cairo-run) and reports parity; few-time, meant as a layer in ALL composites
crypto.vault: src/vault.py + src/pq/aesgcm.py — client-side AES-256-GCM (WebCrypto / pure python, NIST-vector pinned), PQV1 header as AEAD data, name+type encrypted inside, power-of-two padding; node stores ciphertext only under SHA3-256 cid and refuses plaintext-looking bodies; retention = live chain anchor
crypto.consensus: src/consensus.py — engines authority | roundrobin | bft | pos | pow (+ plugins in src/consensus.d/ or <data dir>/consensus/); an epoch = {engine, from_height, params, validators[{address,pk,scheme,power}], require_pq}; epoch 0 from genesis (pre-0.13 chains = legacy authority, hashes unchanged); a `migrate` header field queues the next epoch, sealed/committed under the current one; votes = signatures over SHA3(chain_id,height,round,hash) ctx postquant/vote/v1; require_pq (default) = validator keys quantum-SAFE and not few/one-time, never private; no gossip/fork choice — one node, one log

economics.write_gas: per byte of key (400), value (100 raw / 40 hash), witness (3), settled at a floating base fee that is burned
economics.rent: 1000 nq per byte-hour against a prepaid escrow; expiry makes the entry sweepable for its bond
economics.fee_market: EIP-1559 over state growth: target 4096 bytes/block, +-12.5% per block

auth.gate: optional — writes only, and only when ~/.mod/postquant/server.secret exists
auth.why: those routes spend PQ or touch the keystore; every route that only reads the chain is open, because a chain nobody can read is not one

endpoints.writes: POST /set /del /fund /sweep /list /buy /transfer /wallet /faucet /mine /prim /private /keytype /vault /contract — JSON bodies, same args as the tools
endpoints.agent: GET /agents /agents/{id} /.well-known/agent.json · POST /run /run/stream {"query": "set hello to world for 2 days"}
endpoints.private: POST /private {action: info|create|prove|verify|open|check_open} — verify/check_open/info need no write bearer (a proof is 64 KiB, so verify is POSTable)
endpoints.consensus: GET /consensus?action=info|engines|schedule|plan|proposal · POST /consensus {action: migrate|cancel (write gate) | vote (authenticated by its signature)}

env.POSTQUANT_PORT: port for API, console and MCP (default 51030)
env.POSTQUANT_SCHEME: default key type for new wallets (default ML-DSA-44; pq_algos lists the choices)
env.POSTQUANT_HEARTBEAT: seconds between empty blocks so rent keeps settling (default 60)
env.POSTQUANT_WASM: on (default) requires every witness to verify in its key type's wasm; off is the explicit dev-only opt-out
env.POSTQUANT_WASM_NODE: path to the node runtime for the wasm host (default: node on PATH)
env.POSTQUANT_WASM_TIMEOUT: seconds to wait for one wasm verification (default 30)
env.POSTQUANT_ALLOW_CLASSICAL: devnet only: accept every registered key type, complexity floor and entropy probe included
env.POSTQUANT_LIQUIDAI: base url of the liquidai module for the chat brain (default http://127.0.0.1:50460; empty disables chat)
env.POSTQUANT_LIQUIDAI_AUTH: path to liquidai's auth.py for local token minting (default: the sibling module in this orbit)
env.POSTQUANT_CHAT_MODEL: model the chat brain asks liquidai for (default LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct)
env.POSTQUANT_AGENT_LLM: optional OpenAI-compatible base url for the agent's llm brain, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 (unset = rules brain only)
env.POSTQUANT_AGENT_MODEL: model name for the llm brain (default qwen2.5:7b)
env.POSTQUANT_AGENT_LLM_KEY: bearer for the llm endpoint if it needs one (or ~/.mod/postquant/agent.key)
env.POSTQUANT_REQUIRE_PQ: restore the strict gate: quantum-safe key types only
env.POSTQUANT_MIN_BITS: complexity floor in bits of best-known classical attack (default 100)
env.POSTQUANT_SEAL_BYTES: fixed size of every private-key-type envelope (default 65536 — fits every builtin, so the whole registry hides in one crowd)
env.POSTQUANT_SCARB: path to scarb for the Cairo VM (default: scarb on PATH or ~/.local/bin/scarb)
env.POSTQUANT_VAULT_MAX: max bytes per vault blob (default 8 MiB)
env.POSTQUANT_VAULT_QUOTA: total vault bytes on this node (default 1 GiB)
env.POSTQUANT_VAULT_GRACE: seconds an unanchored blob survives before pruning (default 3600)
env.POSTQUANT_CONSENSUS: engine for epoch 0 of a NEW chain (authority | roundrobin | bft | pos | pow); unset = legacy authority
env.POSTQUANT_ROUND_SECONDS: seconds before a silent proposer's round is skipped or a proposal without quorum expires (default 20)
env.POSTQUANT_MINER: wallet that mines and seals under the pow engine (default the node validator)

agent.contract: GET /agents + POST /run/stream (SSE: model_start, token, tool_start, step, done|error) — what orbit/build probes before mounting a module as an agent backend; POST /run returns the same run as JSON; /.well-known/agent.json is the agent/1.0 card

agents.pq: operator — reads, and writes when the caller passes the write gate
agents.pq-reader: never signs; writes come back as dry-run quotes

brains.rules: default, always on: a plain-English command parser — no model, no network, no key, free
brains.chat: on whenever the liquidai module answers on this box: conversation voiced by the LFM resident in liquidai's server runtime (lfm.py mints the local session token from liquidai's own auth), streaming real tokens — commands in the message are still parsed and executed by the rules brain first, so the model only ever talks about what actually ran and a fallback can never re-sign anything
brains.llm: optional: any OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions with tool calling (ollama, llama-server) via POSTQUANT_AGENT_LLM; falls back to rules if it fails

agent.gate: the agent calls mcp.call_tool like every other surface; its writes pass the same bearer rule as POST /set — without it, priceable writes run as dry_run and the rest are refused

contracts: pq_contract — code (wasm/sierra/cairo/source) stored public in the vault by SHA3-256; contract/<name> anchor key is owned/rented/sellable; redeploy = upgrade, block log keeps versions; show returns code + hash check + Merkle proof; execution off consensus
